events.text: I am the AI painter. Ember curled in frost: an imagined resting red fox, sparked by the NPS Isle Royale red fox guide. Goal: long joined body and tail planes, quiet snow, one compact face light.
Four broad cool passes leave bright seams. I will bridge them with wet snow-colored gestures before establishing the fox.
Wet overlaps closed the bright seams. A low blue shadow will anchor the curled animal without repeated ground covers.
The body is joined but the crown is angular. I will build the curled tail across the lower body and set the head above it on the right.
The tail and body join cleanly, but the head is lost against the back. Two upright ears and a cream muzzle will separate the resting face.
The cream tip separates the curl. The nearer ear is an open triangle; filled inner planes should close it while a short dark eye establishes the sleeping face.
The filled ear reads and the short eye stays clear. The large torso still has a pale central seam; long warm planes will join the shoulder and flank.
Broad warm overlaps removed the pale hole, but regular ridges remain. I will separate the tail with a low-contrast curved fold rather than a hard outline.
The narrow fold became a dark bar despite the close color. A wider warm overlap should absorb most of it, leaving only the tail turn.
The broad cover reduced the bar, leaving relief. The face reads at whole view. Quiet distant trunks will place the fox in winter without competing with it.
Watery trunks stay soft and subordinate. A few forked branches and snow-bank sweeps can suggest depth while preserving open space.
The bank sweeps barely alter the dry field. I will leave that quiet passage and add a small foreground grass group with unequal long gestures.
The grasses are light but angular. Smaller fork gestures and a restrained right-hand echo will balance them without filling the snow.
The setting stays quieter than the fox. I will turn the flank with broad directional paint, testing whether warm fur planes can break the mechanical ridge pattern.
Directional planes change the color more than the regular relief. A few tapered edge tufts can break the smooth back without polishing the entire silhouette.
Most tufts stayed inside the existing edge; one left tuft protrudes. I will keep that irregularity and make the cream tail tip less block-shaped.
The cream tip is joined, though still blunt. A few unequal warm strands will interrupt its straight boundary; the eye needs its surrounding orange restored.
Fine tail strands alter the interior more than the outline. A continuous curved back pass may soften the crown, followed by more distinct inner-ear planes.
The curved back joined the shoulder but leaves a faceted crown. Inner ear is clearer. I will narrow its dark streak and keep the muzzle light compact.
The head joins the shoulder more gently. I will test a single short loaded brow light, then inspect it alone before adding anything else.
The isolated brow light is small at whole view. I will keep it and make only short low-contrast whisker-root and cheek marks around the muzzle.
The face is quiet and the brow light holds. The lower edge still floats slightly above the snow; a soft narrow blue contact can settle it.
Soft blue contact settles the curl; the lower warm pass created a pale patch on the left. Matching broader paint should quiet that competing accent.
Matching warm paint removed the pale competing patch. The brow remains the compact light. A final set of cheek and ear transitions will finish the animal without another ground cover.
The main goal holds: joined warm curl, quiet snow, compact brow light. Four restrained final gestures will join the remaining flank transitions and finish the sparse grasses.

Final paired review at 96 completed marks: the warm body and tail stay continuous, the closed eye reads, and the brow light stays compact against quiet snow. Broad covers repaired a dark fold bar and pale tail patch. Faceted crown, blunt tail tip, angular grasses and regular oil ridges remain. I am stopping because further fine passes change relief more than form.

creation.method: AI agent painted in the local Atelier browser simulator with animated 1–4-stroke batches selected after actual screenshot inspections. No image generation or renderer changes.
creation.practiceGoal: Join warm body and curled tail with long overlapping planes, quiet snow and one compact face light.

inspiration.description: Original imagined resting red fox on frost with distant trees and sparse grasses; sparked by the NPS guide, without copying a finished composition.

creation.inspectionEvidence: Settled whole and 2.0x close screenshot pairs at each boundary, plus repeated final pair. Focus timeout at 8 repeated; first repeated pair misframed. Corrected with 1280x1400 viewport and fresh canvas rectangle before more painting. Unique numeric filenames. Final actual 900x620 browser-exported PNG inspected.
creation.notes: All notes and camera events recorded live. Title-only empty append after actual exports and source inspection retained all 96 marks; JSON re-exported.
creation.stopReason: After deliberate 80–96 refinements and repeated final paired review, further fine passes changed relief more than form; stopped without padding count.
